name: Baana
overview: Baana was a male figure known as one of King Solomon's twelve deputies, specifically overseeing the region of Asher. His role as a deputy indicates a position of administrative responsibility during Solomon's reign. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional notes about his life.
namesAndTitles: The name Baana means 'son of affliction' in Hebrew. This proper name is recorded in 1 Kings 4:16 and was not given directly by God. The meaning of his name reflects a personal or familial background but is not further explained in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Baana is identified as the son of Hushai, as explicitly stated in 1 Kings 4:16. Beyond this father-son relationship, Scripture does not provide additional family details about Baana.
scriptureSignificance: Baana's significance lies in his administrative role under King Solomon, serving as one of the twelve deputies responsible for managing the kingdom's territories. His oversight of Asher highlights the organized governance Solomon established to maintain order and support the nation. Baana's mention, though brief, contributes to the biblical record of Solomon's wise and structured rule.
